newsitem.title: INDIA: India wheat buying from farmers seen at 9.5 mln T.
newsitem.headline: India wheat buying from farmers seen at 9.5 mln T.

text.p: Indian agencies are likely to buy about 9.5 million tonnes of wheat from farmers for sale in the 1997/98 (April-March) season against 8.2 million in the previous year, Agriculture Minister Chaturanan Mishra said on Wednesday.
"Total procurement may be about 9.5 million tonnes," Mishra told a news conference in the Indian capital.
The government buys wheat from farmers to build up buffer stocks and can then control prices by releasing grain through its distribution system.
Food Minister Raghuvansh Prasad Singh later told the news conference that until Wednesday, agencies had procured 9.17 million tonnes of wheat from farmers.

After protests from farmers, India decided in April to pay a 600 rupees ($16.76) per tonne bonus for wheat in addition to the minimum price of 4,150 rupees. The bonus would be paid until June 30 for wheat bought by the government.
Singh said the foodgrains situation was currently "comfortable" after an upward revison of output.

An Agriculture Ministry statement said foodgrains output in 1996/97 (July-June) was estimated at 198.17 million tonnes compared to 185.04 million in the previous season. It was earlier estimated at 192.12 million.
The statement also said that wheat output in 1996/97 was expected at 68.71 million tonnes, up from 62.62 million in the previous crop year. The earlier forecast was 64.66 million tonnes.
